charts.title: Held-out skill as variables are added, target by target.
charts.takeaway: Skill rose with added variables in all 8 targets in the result file and the full model beat its shuffled-target control in 8 of 8. The eighth target, image preference, was built on a private image collection; the paper's text leaves it out and counts seven. Forecaster accuracy flattened at R2 0.131 with all 1,349 variables.
charts.units: held-out skill above chance, in each target's own unit; higher is better. Held-out skill: how well the model predicts cases it was not fitted on. It is R2 (share of variance explained) for numeric targets, AUC (the chance a random positive case ranks above a random negative one) for tree death and image preference, and accuracy for triplets. Chance is 0 for R2, 0.5 for AUC and one in three for triplets
charts.n: Similarity triplets 150,000 cases; Mood at the next beep 8,141 cases; Music valence 1,744 cases; Music arousal 1,744 cases; Forecaster accuracy 2,120 cases; Tree growth 73,553 cases; Tree death 90,427 cases; Image preference 2,625 cases
charts.no_interval: The curves are one informed order and the mean of 8 random orders, with no interval for each point in this chart. The spread of the plateau over the 8 orders is in the result file.
charts.baseline: Shuffled target: the training targets were permuted, the model refitted and scored on the real held-out targets. It should stay at chance
charts.threshold: The full model had to beat the 95th percentile of 20 shuffled-target refits in every target

charts.title: How much of each target's ceiling the full model reached.
charts.takeaway: 1 of 6 targets reached 0.8 of its ceiling, where the forecast was at least 4: similarity triplets at 0.985. Mood stopped at 0.65 and forecaster accuracy at 0.18.
charts.units: share of ceiling: skill above chance divided by the ceiling above chance, where the ceiling is the best score the target's own measurement noise allows, estimated from repeats of the target. 1 means the model predicts as well as the noise permits
charts.n: Similarity triplets 150,000 cases; Mood at the next beep 8,141 cases; Music valence 1,744 cases; Music arousal 1,744 cases; Forecaster accuracy 2,120 cases; Tree growth 73,553 cases
charts.no_interval: The result file gives one share for each target, with no interval. The music ceilings assume 10 raters for each clip.
charts.baseline: A share of 0 is chance and a share of 1 is the noise ceiling
charts.threshold: A target counts as at its ceiling at a share of 0.8 or more; the forecast was at least 4 of 6 targets
charts.ruled_out: The forecast that most targets sit near their ceiling: 5 of 6 fell short of 0.8. The tree growth ceiling came out at −3.96, outside the possible range, so that share has no meaning

axis.label: share of ceiling reached (higher is closer to the noise limit)

charts.title: What one variable of a different kind adds to the full model.
charts.takeaway: Past accuracy lifted forecaster skill from 0.131 to 0.360 and prior growth lifted tree growth from 0.396 to 0.639. 1 of 7 plateaus moved by the rule, where the forecast was at least 3.
charts.units: held-out skill in each target's own unit (R2 or AUC, named in the row); higher is better. Held-out skill: how well the model predicts cases it was not fitted on. It is R2 (share of variance explained) for numeric targets, AUC (the chance a random positive case ranks above a random negative one) for tree death and image preference, and accuracy for triplets
charts.n: Tree growth 73,553 cases; Forecaster accuracy 2,120 cases; Image preference 2,625 cases; Music arousal 1,744 cases; Music valence 1,744 cases; Mood at the next beep 8,141 cases; Tree death 90,427 cases
charts.no_interval: Each end of a row is one held-out score, with no interval in the result file. The rule compares the new score with the plateau's interval over the 8 random orders.
charts.baseline: The full model with every ordinary variable
charts.threshold: A plateau counts as moved when the new score is above the upper end of the plateau's interval; the forecast was at least 3 of 7 targets
charts.ruled_out: The forecast that a new kind of variable moves most plateaus by the rule: 6 of 7 did not. Tree growth gained 0.243 but its plateau interval ran to the fit bound of 2.0, so the rule could not pass
charts.b_name: plus one variable of a different kind

charts.title: Lorenz toy: how far ahead a forecast holds as the starting measurement gets more precise.
charts.takeaway: Each tenfold gain in precision bought 2.51 more time units of forecast, against 2.54 from theory. Twelve decades of precision moved the horizon from 1.2 to 28.7 time units.
charts.units: forecast horizon: the model time until a run started from a slightly wrong state drifts away from the true run, median over starting states, in Lorenz time units; higher is a longer usable forecast
charts.n: 100 starting states at each of 12 precisions; 0 runs never diverged
charts.no_interval: The result file gives the median horizon at each precision, with no interval for each point.
charts.baseline: Theory line: slope 2.543 time units per tenfold gain, set by how fast nearby runs separate in the Lorenz system. The line is drawn through the first measured point
charts.threshold: Straight-line fit with R2 of 0.98 or more, and a slope between 0.75 and 1.25 of the theory slope
charts.planted: The known law was recovered: measured slope over theory slope 0.988, straight-line R2 0.99994

x.label: precision of the starting state (decimal digits; each step is ten times more precise)

y.label: median forecast horizon (time units; higher is longer)
